source_text:
Ἁπλῶς δ’ εἰπεῖν, ὅπερ ἐστὶν σώματι ψυχή, τοῦτ̓ εἰσὶν ἐν κόσμῳ Χριστιανοί.
ἔσπαρται κατὰ πάντων τῶν τοῦ σώματος μελῶν ἡ ψυχή, καὶ Χριστιανοὶ κατὰ τὰς τοῦ κόσμου πόλεις.
οἰκεῖ μὲν ἐν τῷ σώματι ψυχή, οὐκ ἔστι δὲ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος: καὶ Χριστιανοὶ ἐν κόσμῳ οἰκοῦσιν, οὐκ εἰσὶ δὲ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.
ἀόρατος ἡ ψυχὴ ἐν ὁρατῷ φρουρεῖται τῷ σώματι: καὶ Χριστιανοὶ γινώσκονται μὲν ὄντες ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, ἀόρατος δὲ αὐτῶν ἡ θεοσέβεια μένει.
μισεῖ τὴν ψυχὴν ἡ σὰρξ καὶ πολεμεῖ μηδὲν ἀδικουμένη, διότι ταῖς ἡδοναῖς κωλύεται χρῆσθαι: μισεῖ καὶ Χριστιανοὺς ὁ κόσμος μηδὲν ἀδικούμενος, ὅτι ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ἀντιτάσσονται.
ἡ ψυχὴ τὴν μισοῦσαν ἀγαπᾷ σάρκα καὶ τὰ μέλη: καὶ Χριστιανοὶ τοὺς μισοῦντας ἀγαπῶσιν.
ἐγκέκλεισται μὲν ἡ ψυχὴ τῷ σώματι, συνέχει δὲ αὐτὴ τὸ σῶμα: καὶ Χριστιανοὶ κατέχονται μὲν ὡς ἐν φρουρᾷ τῷ κόσμῳ, αὐτοὶ δὲ συνέχουσι τὸν κόσμον.
ἀθάνατος ἡ ψυχὴ ἐν θνητῷ σκηνώματι κατοικεῖ: καὶ Χριστιανοὶ παροικοῦσιν ἐν φθαρτοῖς, τὴν ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἀφθαρσίαν προσδεχόμενοι.
κακουργουμένη σιτίοις καὶ ποτοῖς ἡ ψυχὴ βελτιοῦται: καὶ Χριστιανοὶ κολαζόμενοι καθ̓ ἡμέραν πλεονάζουσι μᾶλλον.
εἰς τοσαύτην αὐτοὺς τάξιν ἔθετο ὁ θεός, ἣν οὐ θεμιτὸν αὐτοῖς παραιτήσασθαι.
thought_title: Christians in the world as the soul in the body
orientation: The author is explaining to Diognetus how Christians relate to the world, using the soul's relation to the body as an extended analogy.
pass_a_gloss: Simply [speaking] to say, what the soul is to the body, this Christians are in the world. The soul is scattered throughout all the members of the body, and Christians throughout the cities of the world. The soul dwells in the body, but is not of the body; and Christians dwell in the world, but are not of the world. The invisible soul is guarded in the visible body; and Christians are known being in the world, but their piety remains invisible. The flesh hates the soul and makes war, being wronged in nothing, because it is prevented from using pleasures; the world hates Christians too, being wronged in nothing, because they oppose the pleasures. The soul loves the flesh that hates it and the members; and Christians love those who hate them. The soul is shut up in the body, but it holds the body together; and Christians are held as in a garrison in the world, but they hold the world together. The immortal soul dwells in a mortal tent; and Christians sojourn in corruptible things, awaiting the incorruption in the heavens. The soul, being maltreated with foods and drinks, is improved; and Christians, being punished daily, increase more. God placed them in so great a rank, which it is not lawful for them to decline.

choices.term: ὅπερ ἐστὶν σώματι ψυχή, τοῦτ̓ εἰσὶν ἐν κόσμῳ Χριστιανοί
choices.english: what the soul is to the body, this Christians are in the world
choices.why: Keeps the demonstrative force of τοῦτ̓ and the dative of relation, preserving the analogy's exact structure.
rejected: Christians are in the world what the soul is in the body

choices.why: The perfect passive of σπείρω suggests a completed sowing with ongoing result; 'is scattered' keeps the agricultural image and the passive voice.

choices.term: οὐκ ἔστι δὲ ἐκ τοῦ σώματος
choices.english: but is not of the body
choices.why: The preposition ἐκ with the genitive indicates origin or source; 'of' preserves this nuance better than 'from' in English idiom.
rejected: but is not from the body

choices.why: The passive of φρουρέω means to be kept under guard or protection; 'is guarded' captures the protective sense without implying imprisonment.
The middle voice of ἀντιτάσσω means to set oneself against; 'they oppose' keeps the active resistance implied by the middle.
φρουρά means a military guard-post or garrison; the simile suggests protective custody rather than a prison, which fits the parallel with the soul being guarded in the body.

pass_b_english: To put it simply, Christians are to the world what the soul is to the body.
The soul is scattered through all the members of the body, and Christians are scattered through the cities of the world.
The soul dwells in the body, but it is not of the body; and Christians dwell in the world, but they are not of the world.
The invisible soul is guarded within the visible body; and Christians are known to be in the world, yet their piety remains invisible.

The flesh hates the soul and makes war on it, though it has suffered no wrong, because the soul keeps it from enjoying its pleasures; and the world hates Christians, though it has suffered no wrong, because they oppose its pleasures.
The soul loves the flesh that hates it, and its members; and Christians love those who hate them.
The soul is shut up in the body, yet it holds the body together; and Christians are held in the world as in a garrison, yet they hold the world together.
The immortal soul dwells in a mortal tent; and Christians live as resident aliens among corruptible things, awaiting the incorruption that is in heaven.
When the soul is mistreated with food and drink, it improves; and when Christians are punished daily, they increase all the more.
God has placed them in so great a rank, which it is not lawful for them to refuse.

problems.why: Different words used for the same idea of Christians as outsiders.
problems.fix: Standardise on one term, e.g., “resident aliens.”

problems.quote: When the soul is mistreated with food and drink, it improves;
problems.why: Logical contradiction; mistreatment cannot improve the soul.
problems.fix: Replace with “When the soul is disciplined in food and drink, it is refined.”

problems.why: Christians are called 'resident aliens' in sections 5-6 but 'foreigners' in section 5; reader may miss the parallel.
problems.fix: Use 'resident aliens' consistently or note the synonym.

problems.quote: Christians are held in the world as in a garrison
problems.why: 'Garrison' suggests a military installation; the Greek likely means 'prison' or 'place of detention,' fitting the soul-in-body analogy.

edits.new: Christians are held in the world as in a prison

problems.quote: They live in their own homelands, but as resident aliens
problems.why: The same Greek concept (paroikos) is rendered 'resident aliens' and 'foreigners' in the same section.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, or note that 'foreigners' restates 'resident aliens.'

problems.quote: When the soul is disciplined with food and drink, it is refined
problems.why: 'Disciplined with food and drink' is ambiguous; the context likely means 'by fasting' (deprivation), not being given food and drink.
problems.fix: Render as 'when the soul is disciplined by withholding food and drink' or similar.

edits.new: When the soul is disciplined by withholding food and drink, it is refined;

The mistranslation about 'disciplined with food and drink' has been corrected to clarify that the discipline is by withholding food and drink.

problems.fix: Use one term consistently for the alien-resident paradox.
